svg.text: Logistic regression was born in 1958, right in the middle of this stream

tspan.tspan: 1936, LDA (Linear Discriminant Analysis):
Proposed by Ronald Fisher. A statistical method
that finds the axis maximizing between-class variance while minimizing within-class variance.
1951, KNN (K-Nearest Neighbors):
Proposed by Fix and Hodges. A non-parametric method that
classifies based on the nearest neighboring data, with no complicated equations.
1957, the Perceptron:
The first artificial neural network model, developed by Frank
Rosenblatt. It could only do simple linear classification, so it hit a wall on the XOR
problem.
1958, Logistic Regression:
The theory of computing class-membership probability in a
mathematically rigorous way, grounded in probability (likelihood).
1979/1984, Decision Trees (ID3 & CART):
Algorithms that look for the rule which reduces
impurity (entropy, Gini index) the most when splitting the data. They produce IF-THEN rules
people can read, and started to see wide practical use.
1986, MLP & Backpropagation:
With hidden layers and the backpropagation algorithm, models
broke past the perceptron’s linear-classification limit and began learning non-linear decision
boundaries.

svg.text: The age of mathematical optimization and ensembles

tspan.tspan: 1995, SVM (Support Vector Machine):
Proposed by Vladimir Vapnik. By introducing 'margin
maximization' and the 'kernel trick', it outperformed neural networks on non-linear
classification of high-dimensional data, and reigned as the king of machine learning until the
early 2000s.
1995 – 2001, Random Forest:
To stop the chronic overfitting of a single decision tree, the
bagging ensemble technique was established: build many trees independently and let them vote
by majority.

svg.text: The evolution of boosting and the deep learning renaissance

tspan.tspan: 2001, GBM (Gradient Boosting Machine):
Proposed by Jerome Friedman. It established
boosting, where each new tree sequentially corrects the previous tree's error (gradient).
2012, CNNs open the deep learning era:
AlexNet crushed the existing algorithms at the
ILSVRC image classification competition, shifting the paradigm for unstructured data (images,
text, audio) entirely to deep learning.
2014 – 2017, the big three boosters (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost):
Algorithms that pushed
GBM’s speed and overfitting problems to their optimized limit. To this day they sweep tabular
data classification competitions (Kaggle and friends) as the practical state of the art.
